checks_passed.check: arithmetic - independent re-derivation of the des-chloro claim
checks_passed.what_was_verified: Recomputed every mass/mole pair and every mass-versus-yield closure from the printed text and the drawn structures, using standard atomic weights and without reference to the annotation. CONFIRMED. Steps 1-4 sit in a des-chloro regime: implied MWs are short of the drawn compound by 34.43 (step 1 product, 28.6 g / 0.168 mol = 170.24 vs C8H9ClO2S 204.67), 34.67 and 34.49 (step 2 substrate and product), 34.70 (step 3 substrate) and 34.68 / 34.86 (step 4 substrate and product), against Cl - H = 34.44; the implied values 170.2, 212.2, 214.0 and 227.8 match the des-chloro analogues 170.23, 212.26, 214.23 and 228.26. The annotation's per-step numbers agree with mine to the second decimal in every case.

checks_passed.check: arithmetic - independent re-derivation of the 44.7 claim
checks_passed.what_was_verified: CONFIRMED, and it is broader than the substrate charges the annotation names. Shortfalls against the drawn compound: step 5 substrate 44.70 and product 44.46; step 6 product 44.53; step 7 substrate 44.70 and product 45.16; step 8 substrate 44.81 and product 45.02. From the step-4 product onward every printed figure except one sits 44.5-45.2 below the drawn structure. The one exception is step 6's substrate charge, 55.8 g / 0.2 mol = 279.0 against C10H10BrClO4S 341.60, short by 62.60, which fits neither regime and also breaks the patent's own chain (step 5's product figures imply 297.14 for the same compound). The annotation records all of these numbers correctly and does note the 302 and 396 internal self-consistency; it does not state the product-side 44.5 offset as a single pattern, which is a framing point, not an error.

CONFIRMED independently. 82 g against 0.24 mol input at C9H9ClO4S 248.68 is 137.4% of the theoretical maximum at complete conversion, and mass plus yield imply MW 474.54, which matches no species in the reaction and does not close against the patent's own des-chloro weight either (0.24 x 214.23 x 0.72 = 37.0 g). This is the only step whose printed mass exceeds its own theoretical maximum, and the annotation identifies it as such.

The handover from step 4 to step 5 assigns two different weights to the same compound: step 4's product closes at 227.84 (des-chloro) while step 5's charge implies 218.00 (true minus 44.70), a 9.84 g/mol internal contradiction. The annotation records this in Example 1_Step 4 notes.
